why: I compared each check's PASS/FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 hold. Check 1 only tests that clamp is exported and clamps values. Check 2 only tests that a RangeError is thrown when lo > hi. Check 4 only needs `npm test` to exit 0. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS needs "the script reports nothing missing", and the script counts a function as documented only if README.md matches the regex `\bname\s*\(`, meaning the name followed by a parenthesis. "README.md documents every function math.js exports" does not require that format. For example, a README entry like "subtract — returns a minus b" documents subtract but would fail. That is an exact-wording rule the words don't force, and it sits in a PASS/FAIL condition instead of under Advisory.
